info.title: Estimator9 API
info.description:
IFRS 9 provisioning engine — MEV series, model fitting, and the accounts that drive them.

Obtain a token from `POST /auth/login` and send it as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. Endpoints marked with a padlock require one; those that also need a permission list it under their 403 response.

Tokens are short-lived and carry the caller's permissions, so a role changed after sign-in takes effect on the next token rather than the next request.

post.summary: Exchange an email and password for an access token.
post.description:
Rejections are deliberately indistinguishable: an unknown address, a wrong
password and a disabled account all return the same 401. Anything else
would let a caller enumerate accounts.

The single exception is a locked account, which returns 423 — but only to a
caller who supplied the *correct* password, and so has already confirmed
the account exists. Someone guessing still sees 401.

400.description: The body is not valid JSON

401.description: Invalid credentials — indistinguishable from an unknown, locked or disabled account

422.description: Email or password rejected by policy

423.description: The password was correct but the account is temporarily locked after repeated failures

503.description: The data store is unavailable; retry

post.summary: End the session and clear the refresh cookie.
post.description:
Needs no access token: a caller whose access token has already expired must
still be able to log out. Always succeeds — an unknown token still means
"log me out", and saying otherwise would reveal whether it was real.

get.description:
Needs no permission — every authenticated caller may read their own
account, and Angular calls this on boot to render a header and decide which
navigation to show. It re-reads from the database rather than echoing the
token, so a name changed since login is current.

401.description: Missing, malformed or expired access token

503.description: The data store is unavailable; retry

patch.description:
Name only: the email address is the login identifier, and changing it
unverified turns one typo into a locked-out account. That goes through an
administrator.

400.description: The body is not valid JSON

401.description: Missing, malformed or expired access token

503.description: The data store is unavailable; retry

post.description:
Requires the current password even though the caller already holds a valid
token — a token is something a borrowed laptop already has, and this is the
operation that would lock its owner out.

Every session ends, including this one, and a fresh session is returned. So
the caller stays signed in and every other device is signed out, which is
the point of changing a password you think someone else may know.

200.description: Changed; a replacement session is returned and all others are ended

400.description: The body is not valid JSON

401.description: Missing token, or the current password is wrong

422.description: The new password does not meet policy

503.description: The data store is unavailable; retry

post.summary: Ask for a password reset link.
post.description:
**Always returns 204**, whether or not the address belongs to an account.
Reporting "no such user" would turn this into a way to ask whether someone
holds an account here — a leak that needs no credentials at all.

Rate limited: without it, this endpoint sends mail to any address a caller
names, as often as they like.

204.description: Accepted. A link is sent only if the address has an active account, and the response is identical either way

400.description: The body is not valid JSON

422.description: That is not a valid email address

503.description: The data store is unavailable; retry

post.summary: Redeem a reset link and set a new password.
post.description:
Unknown, expired and already-used tokens all answer 401 alike — telling
them apart would say whether a link was ever real.

No session is returned: the user logs in afterwards. Signing them in here
would mean a link forwarded to the wrong inbox grants a live session rather
than only the chance to set a password.

204.description: Password set and every session ended; sign in again

400.description: The body is not valid JSON

401.description: The token is unknown, expired, or already used

422.description: The new password does not meet policy

503.description: The data store is unavailable; retry

post.summary: Exchange the refresh cookie for a new access token.
post.description:
The old refresh token is revoked and replaced, so each one is usable
exactly once. Presenting an already-used token ends the whole session — see
[`application::identity::RefreshSession`].

Takes no request body: the credential is the httpOnly cookie, which script
cannot read and the browser attaches automatically.

401.description: Missing, expired, or already-used refresh token. Reuse ends the whole session

503.description: The data store is unavailable; retry

get.description:
Reports the running binary's version. Does not touch the database — a 200
here means the process is up, not that it can serve data.

get.summary: List every permission the system checks for.
get.description:
Reference data: it changes with a release, not through the API, because a
permission nothing in the code checks would be a label that grants nothing.

401.description: Missing, malformed or expired access token

503.description: The data store is unavailable; retry

get.summary: List the roles that can be assigned.
get.description:
Includes `superadmin`, flagged, so a UI can show it as unassignable rather
than offering it and taking a 403.

401.description: Missing, malformed or expired access token

503.description: The data store is unavailable; retry

get.description:
Ordered by id ascending. Not paginated — the user table is small by design;
pagination arrives if and when it stops being.

401.description: Missing, malformed or expired access token

403.description: Authenticated but lacks users.read — retrying will not help

503.description: The data store is unavailable; retry

post.description:
The password is supplied by the administrator and must meet the same policy
as any other — length only, no composition rules. `superadmin` cannot be
granted here; that is the vendor's account, not one a client administrator
mints.

201.description: Created; the Location header names the new account

400.description: The body is not valid JSON

401.description: Missing, malformed or expired access token

403.description: Lacks users.manage, or attempted to grant superadmin

404.description: A named role does not exist

409.description: That email address is already in use

422.description: Email, name, password or role name rejected

503.description: The data store is unavailable; retry

401.description: Missing, malformed or expired access token

403.description: Authenticated but lacks users.read — retrying will not help

503.description: The data store is unavailable; retry

delete.description:
Not a delete: the row is retained so the audit trail keeps pointing at a
real account. Live sessions are closed and refresh tokens revoked in the
same transaction, so the account cannot obtain a new access token. One
already issued stays valid until it expires — at most the access-token
lifetime.

401.description: Missing, malformed or expired access token

403.description: Lacks users.manage, or targeted yourself or a superadmin

404.description: No such user, or it is already inactive

503.description: The data store is unavailable; retry

patch.summary: Change a user's name or address.
patch.description:
Partial: omit a field to leave it alone. An empty body is a 422 rather than
a silent success, since it is almost always a client bug.

Roles are not editable here — they have their own endpoint, with their own
escalation rails.

400.description: The body is not valid JSON

401.description: Missing, malformed or expired access token

403.description: Lacks users.manage, or targeted a superadmin

409.description: That email address is already in use

422.description: Nothing to change, or the address is malformed

503.description: The data store is unavailable; retry

put.description:
The list is exhaustive: whatever is sent becomes the user's complete set,
and an empty list removes every role. A PATCH-style add/remove would make
concurrent edits silently lose one another.

`superadmin` cannot be granted or removed here, and nobody may change their
own roles — both would let a holder of `users.manage` escalate past every
other boundary.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The user whose roles are being replaced

400.description: The body is not valid JSON

401.description: Missing, malformed or expired access token

403.description: Lacks users.manage, or attempted to change own roles or a superadmin

404.description: No such user, or a named role does not exist

503.description: The data store is unavailable; retry

get.summary: List the software features and whether they are enabled.
get.description:
Vendor only. A client administrator gets 403 however privileged they are —
there is no permission that grants this, deliberately.

401.description: Missing, malformed or expired access token

500.description: The stored feature state is unreadable or has been tampered with

put.summary: Enable or disable a feature for this installation.
put.description:
Vendor only, and audited with `via_superadmin` so the change is visible to
the client's auditor even though it never touches their database.

Setting a feature to the state it already has does nothing and records
nothing.

400.description: The body is not valid JSON

401.description: Missing, malformed or expired access token

404.description: This release has no such feature

500.description: The stored feature state is unreadable or has been tampered with

AssignRolesRequest.description: The complete set of roles the user should end up with.

roles.description: Exhaustive, not additive — an empty list removes every role.

ChangePasswordRequest.description: A password change. Both values go through the same policy check.

password.description: At least 12 characters. Never echoed back and never audited.

roles.description:
May be empty; the account then has no permissions until roles are
assigned.

ErrorResponse.description:
The body every failing request returns. One shape for all errors, so a
client can parse failures without branching on the status code.

error.description: Human-readable description of what went wrong.

description.example: Fit MEV regression models from macroeconomic series.

enabled_by_default.description:
What a fresh installation would have. Useful when deciding whether a
state was set deliberately or has simply never been touched.

ResetPasswordRequest.description: The token from the emailed link, plus the password to set.

RoleResponse.description: A role the administrator can assign.

description.description:
What holding it means. The only place that explains a role to someone
who did not define it, so it is published rather than kept internal.
description.example: Fits MEV models and reviews results.

is_superadmin.description:
True for the vendor account, which sits outside the permission model.
Published so a UI can show it as unassignable rather than offering it
and taking a 403.

SessionResponse.description:
Returned by both `/auth/login` and `/auth/refresh` — the same thing is
being handed over in each case.

expires_at.description:
When the token stops being accepted. Short by design — permissions are
carried inside it, so this bounds how long a revoked role keeps working.

user.description: Saves the client an immediate follow-up call to render a header.

UpdateUserRequest.description: Fields to change. Omit one to leave it alone.

UserResponse.description:
A user as the API publishes them.

There is deliberately no password field of any kind. Because `User` keeps
its hash private and this struct is written by hand, adding one would have
to be a conscious act rather than a `#[derive(Serialize)]` accident.

is_active.description: Deactivated accounts are retained, not deleted.

is_superadmin.description:
True when the account holds `superadmin` and therefore bypasses every
permission check.

roles.description:
Role names, alphabetically. Permissions are not expanded here — they are
issued in the access token at login.

bearer.description: Issued by POST /auth/login. Expires; refresh by logging in again.

tags.name: roles
tags.description: The authorization vocabulary: roles and the permissions they carry. Read-only — reference data changes with a release, not through the API.

tags.name: identity
tags.description: User accounts. Roles and permissions arrive with the RBAC slice.

tags.name: vendor
tags.description: Vendor-only. Controls which software features this installation may use. Unreachable by any client role, however privileged — these are not the client's decisions to make.
